e8b_medium_ledger.scope: every MEDIUM and LOW finding from the three review lenses of the previous round, plus findings raised in this session, each classified and dispositioned. No finding is silently dismissed.

classification_rules.execution-critical: must be fixed before any core training
classification_rules.scientific-validity: must be fixed, or proven not to affect the frozen primary protocol
classification_rules.provenance/reproducibility: must be fixed where it affects reconstruction
classification_rules.reporting/documentation: may remain only if scheduled for dissertation cleanup and cannot mislead execution

entries.issue: Frozen LM training-path numerics change bf16->fp32 under autocast; A1_precision said training 'unchanged' and nothing pinned the LM training dtype
entries.evidence: build_core_recipe now carries training_precision AND frozen_lm_instance_dtype explicitly, both inside recipe_sha256. Under bf16 autocast every per-op operand is the exactly-representable pinned bf16 value, so the training math equals the pinned-bf16 construction; this is stated in the recipe rather than assumed.

entries.issue: build_core_recipe still emitted max_epochs 100 and patience 10 for B2/B3, contradicting the fixed-22 decision, and the budget sat outside the hash
entries.evidence: B2/B3 recipes now carry max_epochs 22, early_stopping False, patience 'disabled', canonical_checkpoint_rule epoch_22 and primary_checkpoint_selection fixed_endpoint, all INSIDE recipe_sha256. Protocol family bumped to e8b-fp32-fixed22-core-2026-08-07 so any earlier recipe/checkpoint fails resume.

entries.issue: assert_lm_buffer_parity had no runnable call site; the OI5 pair check never executed
entries.evidence: Called in preflight on the two live inventories AND in _train_core_locked for every B2/B3 cell, comparing this arm against its counterpart, after construction and before the first optimizer step.

entries.issue: Fixing the epoch count equalises draws but not max-over-epochs selection bias (~0.008-0.010/cell), which does not cancel in B3-B2; no selection-free estimator planned
entries.evidence: Superseded by the user's fixed-endpoint decision: the primary checkpoint is epoch 22, not the max over epochs, so there is no max-over-epochs selection bias in the primary contrast at all. Best-of-22 survives only as a labelled secondary diagnostic that cannot determine the primary comparison, the freeze or the clean-test checkpoint. Per-row canonical predictions are dumped for paired tests.

entries.issue: B1 keeps patience-10/max-100 while B2/B3 are fixed, so B1-involving contrasts retain the run-length confound
entries.evidence: The user's decision F is explicit that B1 retains its frozen section 7.3 recipe and must not be forced onto the 22-epoch rule. B1 is an interface-width control, not part of the primary B3-B2 contrast, which is unaffected. The asymmetry is recorded in the recipe (B1 canonical_checkpoint_rule = best dev accuracy, section 7.3 inherited) and in CLAUDE.md.
entries.closed_by: training.py build_core_recipe B1 branch; CLAUDE.md gate item 5

entries.issue: lm.config.dtype and generation_config differed between the paired arms and were covered by no hash or pair check
entries.evidence: load_frozen_causal_lm now normalises config.dtype for both arms and loads generation_config from the pinned snapshot for both, so no frozen state other than the parameter values differs across the pair. Both are recorded in provenance.

entries.issue: Resource projection and abandonment evidence had no committed generator; npz untracked; B1 hours not reproducible

entries.evidence: superseded_evidence_20260807.json now carries 14 records including all four, each with why-wrong and replacement. Source files preserved verbatim; live constants carry the withdrawal.

entries.issue: assert_canonical_scores was vacuous; the frozen-LM dtype check sampled a single parameter
entries.evidence: assert_canonical_scores now also enforces finiteness (a NaN would otherwise pass every threshold and sail through argmax). canonical_prefix checks the FULL dtype set of both the trainable model and the frozen LM, not one sampled parameter.

entries.issue: G14 halt details omitted questionId/imageId; the record omitted the minimum margin
entries.evidence: g14_fp32_gate takes dev_frame and records questionId and imageId in every halt detail; dev_margin_quantiles now includes min.

entries.issue: canonical_prefix's autocast guard did not see CPU autocast
entries.evidence: torch.is_autocast_enabled('cpu') added to the guard.

entries.issue: g14_fp32_gate checked only the length of the supplied margins
entries.evidence: CLOSED 2026-08-07: G14-FP32 now REQUIRES an evaluation binding at the post-selection stage and re-verifies it against the live model, recomputing the model-state digest and the margin digest and halting on any mismatch. The binding carries the model-state digest, recipe SHA, protocol family, evaluation precision, prediction and margin digests, row count and scorer source digest, so a record whose margins cannot be proven to belong to the evaluated state fails closed.
entries.closed_by: training.py evaluation_binding + g14_fp32_gate binding re-verification; known-negative tests

entries.issue: The G8 overfit gate trains to a convergence threshold and so consumes a different number of RNG draws in B2 than in B3. The paired arms therefore entered the training loop on divergent global RNG states, so their dropout masks and shuffle orders differed for a reason unrelated to the pretrained-versus-random contrast that B3 minus B2 exists to isolate. The loader generator was re-seeded after the gate; the global RNG was not.
entries.evidence: training.py re-seeds with e8b_run.reseed_strict(recipe['seed']) after the G8/G14 gates and before the resume block, so both arms enter training on a common RNG state; the placement before the resume block preserves resume fidelity, since a resume legitimately overwrites RNG from the saved state. Ordering is asserted in tests (gate < reseed < loop, and reseed < resume).

entries.issue: history, train_times and eval_times were not resume fields. The fixed-endpoint rule reads history[-1] to identify the epoch-22 canonical checkpoint, so a cell resumed at or near the final epoch would die on an IndexError inside a loop that would then retry and die again, or would select a canonical epoch from a truncated record.
entries.evidence: run.RESUME_FIELDS now carries history, train_times and eval_times; save_resume_checkpoint requires them and restore_resume_state returns them; training.py restores them on resume. The empty-history path halts through gate_halt with the reason stated instead of raising IndexError. Superseded pre-amendment checkpoints stay READABLE FOR AUDIT via protocol_family=None but cannot be restored, which is asserted as a known negative.
